coverage_argument.purpose: This independent question suite tests whether an answer system can resolve legally material M&A exclusivity questions from the governing agreement without treating a sample term as a default.
coverage_argument.coverage_rule: Every question is decomposed into answer slots. A compliant answer must resolve every applicable slot from operative language, controlling definitions and required cross-references, or state that the agreement does not express the point.
covered_dimensions: existence, agreement relationship and subject-matter scope
bound parties, representatives, beneficiaries and enforcement recipients
start, end, expiry, survival, time zone and track transitions
outbound solicitation, information, access, discussion, negotiation, assistance, approval and competing-agreement activity
past-contact shut-down, data return and standstill treatment
inbound receipt, clarification, notice, notice contents and continuing updates
competing-proposal and superior-proposal definitions, thresholds and comparison factors
fiduciary-out, adviser, legal-duty, confidentiality, financing-source and no-breach conditions
matching rights, counterproposals, response periods, resets and material amendments
recommendation changes, tender offers, intervening events and termination for a superior proposal
go-shop permissions, excluded-party status, expiry and differential fee treatment
public disclosure, amendments, waivers, third-party rights, remedies and drafting
sample_variation_observed: continuing-bidder category after an initial outreach period
board recommendation, termination and matching procedures
coverage_argument.answer_completeness_test: For each user request, identify all implicated questions, then answer every applicable answer slot with section-level evidence. Do not supply missing facts from market practice.
coverage_argument.non_default_rule: The five reviewed public agreements are a challenge-design sample only. They do not establish a rule for a different agreement.

known_limits: This is a five-agreement public SEC sample. It cannot prove coverage of every transaction structure, jurisdiction or negotiated variation.

The source sample contains publicly filed exhibits only. It does not include schedules, confidential side letters, process documents or unfiled amendments unless incorporated in the governing agreement.
The catalogue tests agreement-based answers. It is not a statement of Delaware, federal or other law, and it does not replace fact-specific legal analysis.
A source agreement can use different defined terms, thresholds, time periods and remedies. Each answer must be tied to the agreement being analysed.
The source review was limited to the sealed manifest inputs. No comparison material from any separate catalogue or key set was used.
Questions are intentionally broad enough to surface omissions, but a new transaction type can require a successor challenge catalogue.
